cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: A well‑formed JSON string is supplied with the JSON input format. The method should deserialize the string successfully and return an empty validation result because the instance complies with the schema.

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: A well‑formed YAML document is supplied with the YAML input format. The method should correctly deserialize the YAML and return no validation messages.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing at least one message that indicates a parsing error (e.g., "unexpected token" or "cannot deserialize").
cases.description: The JSON string is syntactically malformed. Deserialization should fail and the validator must return a validation message describing the parse error.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a parsing‑error message for YAML.
cases.description: The YAML document contains an illegal token. The method should catch the parsing exception and surface it as a validation message.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message "Input string cannot be null" (or similar).
cases.description: Passing a null input string should be rejected early, before any deserialization attempt, resulting in an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a parsing error indicating empty content.
cases.description: An empty string cannot be parsed into a JSON node; the method should return a validation message that reflects the inability to deserialize an empty payload.

cases.expected: UnsupportedOperationException (or IllegalArgumentException) stating that the provided InputFormat is not supported.
cases.description: When an input format that the validator does not recognise is supplied, the method should throw an exception rather than attempting deserialization.

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors) after successful URL decoding and JSON deserialization.
cases.description: When the input format indicates URL‑encoded JSON, the method should first decode the string (using UTF‑8) and then validate the resulting JSON. No validation errors are expected for a correct payload.

cases.expected: UnsupportedEncodingException wrapped in a ValidationException or propagated as an IllegalStateException.
cases.description: If URL decoding fails because the underlying charset is not supported, the method should surface the error appropriately (commonly as an unchecked exception).

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a parsing‑error message indicating that the content is empty or cannot be parsed.
cases.description: The input consists only of whitespace characters. After trimming, there is no JSON content, so deserialization should fail and a validation message about empty content is expected.

group: Input with UTF‑8 Byte Order Mark (BOM)

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: A JSON payload prefixed with the UTF‑8 BOM should be correctly recognized and stripped by the deserializer, resulting in successful validation.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or a ValidationMessage indicating a URL‑decoding error).
cases.description: The percent‑encoding is incomplete (trailing ‘%7’). URL decoding should throw an exception which is surfaced as a validation error.

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: When the format indicates URL‑encoded JSON but the payload is plain JSON, the decoder simply returns the original string, allowing normal deserialization and validation.

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: Jackson’s YAML parser can also read pure JSON. Supplying JSON with the YAML format should therefore succeed.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a parsing‑error message because the YAML syntax is not valid JSON.
cases.description: Providing a YAML document while the format is set to JSON should cause a parsing failure and a corresponding validation message.

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: Whitespace surrounding a valid JSON document must be ignored by the deserializer, resulting in successful validation.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing at least one message indicating a type mismatch (e.g., expected object but found array).
cases.description: The schema used by JsonSchema expects an object at the root. Supplying a JSON array should deserialize correctly but later produce a validation message about the wrong type.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a type‑mismatch message because the root node is a null literal, not an object.
cases.description: The string "null" is a valid JSON literal but does not satisfy a schema that expects an object, leading to a validation error.

group: Unicode Characters in JSON String Values

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: JSON strings may contain Unicode characters. The deserializer should handle UTF‑8 correctly and validation should succeed.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException) indicating that the InputFormat argument cannot be null.
cases.description: Passing a non‑null JSON string while the InputFormat argument is null should cause the method to reject the call early, throwing an IllegalArgumentException (or NPE) before any deserialization occurs.
